title: 2011 AMC 12B Problem 6
statement: Two tangents to a circle are drawn from a point \(A.\) The points of contact \(B\) and \(C\) divide the circle into arcs with lengths in the ratio \(2:3.\) What is the degree measure of \(\angle BAC?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(O\) be the center. The arcs measure \(2x\) and \(3x\) with \(2x+3x=360^\circ,\) so \(x=72^\circ\) and the minor arc \(BC\) gives central angle \(\angle BOC=144^\circ.\)

The radii to \(B\) and \(C\) are perpendicular to the tangents, so \(\angle ABO=\angle ACO=90^\circ.\) In quadrilateral \(ABOC,\) \[ \begin{gathered} \angle BAC=360^\circ-144^\circ-90^\circ \\ {}-90^\circ=36^\circ. \end{gathered} \]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The two arcs split \(360^\circ\) in the ratio \(2:3\)
A tangent meets the radius at its point of contact at \(90^\circ\); use quadrilateral \(ABOC\)
